title: Microsoft Q2 FY2025 Earnings Call Transcript

sections.prepared_remarks: Microsoft reporting Q2 revenue of $69.6 billion, up 12 percent year over year. Cloud revenue surpassed $100 billion annualized for the first time. Azure and other cloud services grew 33 percent, with AI services contributing approximately 12 points to that growth. This is the first time AI has driven double-digit contribution to Azure growth — a major inflection point. Copilot for Microsoft 365 now has over 600,000 paying organizations, up from 400,000 last quarter. GitHub Copilot Enterprise grew 50 percent quarter over quarter. We are the leading AI infrastructure provider — more than 60 percent of Fortune 500 companies use Azure OpenAI Service. Our security business hit $20 billion annualized revenue. Windows 11 enterprise deployment is accelerating. Xbox Game Pass grew to over 35 million subscribers. LinkedIn revenue grew 9 percent to $4.4 billion, a record. Our AI strategy is monetizing faster than any prior platform shift in our history. We are continuing to invest aggressively — capex this quarter was $14.9 billion to support AI datacenter buildout.
sections.financial_highlights: EPS $2.93, revenue $69.6 billion, gross margin 72.3 percent. Operating income $27.2 billion, up 15 percent. We generated $29.2 billion in operating cash flow and $23.9 billion in free cash flow. We returned $9.9 billion to shareholders through buybacks and dividends. We expect Q3 revenue of $70.7 to $71.7 billion. Azure growth guidance of 31 to 33 percent for Q3 includes an 8-point AI contribution. Our cloud gross margins expanded 90 basis points sequentially. AI compute utilization rates are improving faster than expected. We are on track to reach $100 billion in annualized cloud revenue in the back half of fiscal 2025. Our supply chain team has secured GPU and networking capacity well ahead of competitors — a structural advantage that will compound over fiscal 2026.
sections.qanda_session:
Keith Bachman: Satya, there's a narrative that OpenAI is taking AI infrastructure business away from Azure. Can you address that directly? And can you help us understand the difference between your Azure OpenAI Service API customers versus your own Copilot customers in terms of monetization velocity?

Satya Nadella: Keith, let me be direct. OpenAI is our strategic partner and our largest Azure customer for AI workloads. Their API business drives substantial Azure compute revenue. On Copilot — our own product layer — that's a different margin profile: higher gross margins because it's proprietary software. Both are growing rapidly and they reinforce each other. The OpenAI partnership gives us model innovation while we focus on the best-in-class inference infrastructure and enterprise distribution. That combination is our competitive moat. We don't see OpenAI as a competitor to Azure AI infrastructure — quite the opposite. The more developers build on OpenAI models, the more they need Azure infrastructure.

Raimo Lenschow: Amy, the capex of $14.9 billion — how should we think about the trajectory over the next several quarters? And is there any way to break out utilization of the new GPU clusters between AI training versus inference workloads?

Amy Hood: Raimo, on capex — we're planning to continue at elevated levels through fiscal 2025 as we scale AI infrastructure ahead of demand. We expect capex to remain in the $14 to $16 billion range for the next two quarters as we bring online additional datacenter capacity in the US, Europe, and Asia. On utilization by workload: we don't break that out in detail, but inference currently represents the majority of GPU compute consumption. Training workloads are growing as we train newer, larger models for Copilot and Azure OpenAI. We expect inference to remain dominant in the near term as model deployment scales, but training demand will grow as customers fine-tune models on proprietary data. Our GPU efficiency is improving — we are getting better utilization per dollar spent through software optimizations and workload scheduling.
sections.forward_outlook: Satya Nadella: We are in the early stages of a major platform shift to AI. Microsoft Copilot is becoming the AI assistant for every role and function. The enterprise adoption curve is steeper than any prior product we have launched. Security, compliance, and enterprise integration are our moats against consumer AI tools. This quarter we saw Record quarterly installs of Microsoft 365 — the bundling of Copilot is driving higher attach rates on Office, Dynamics, and Power Platform. We expect the AI portion of Azure to reach 20 percent contribution by Q4 of this fiscal year. We have the most profitable cloud business in the industry and we are using that cash generation to compound our AI infrastructure advantage.
